title: radio.py: remove_node drops TxEnd without medium.end_tx; TX list leaks
description:
## Problem

`RadioMixin.remove_node` drops delayed-RX stash then calls `NodeManagementMixin.remove_node`, which pops `_active_transmissions` and `EventQueue.remove_events_for_node` (including `TxEndEvent`) **without** `self._medium.end_tx`.

`Medium.get_active_transmissions` filters by `start_time_us <= t < end_time_us`, so the frame still occupies the medium until airtime ends — then the `Transmission` and `_tx_positions` entry stay in `Medium._active_transmissions` forever. Every later `get_rx_candidates` walks the whole list.

`get_active_transmissions` is O(n) over that list on every RX poll (~1 ms, metrics.py docstring; HIL `deliver_pending_packets`). Node churn (failure injection, mobility, `test_remove_node_drops_stash`) therefore leaks medium entries and slows RX.

Related but distinct from closed work:

- 9098.11/15: `_delayed_rx` ghosts (stash TTL). RadioMixin now drops stash on remove; the *medium* list is untouched.
- 9098.22: RX teardown deleting TxEnd/TxStartDelayed. That fixed `remove_events_for_node_of_type`. Full `remove_events_for_node` on node removal still deletes TxEnd, which was correct *if* `end_tx` ran first. It does not.

`_do_start_transmission` already `end_tx`s a superseded TX. The remove path is the missing symmetric cleanup.

## Files

- python/src/lichen/sim/simulation/radio.py (`remove_node` / `_drop_delayed_rx_for_node`)
- python/src/lichen/sim/simulation/nodes.py (`remove_node` pops active TX + events, no end_tx)
- python/src/lichen/sim/events.py (`remove_events_for_node` deletes TxEndEvent)

## Why this is robustness

Long-running sims that add/remove nodes (failure, join/leave, re-flash) grow an unbounded in-memory TX list. RX polling cost and RSSI/collision work scale with historical removed transmitters, not with in-air frames. The 9098.24 metrics caps assumed the radio layer would not leak the same way.
design: In RadioMixin.remove_node (before super): if `_active_transmissions[node_id]` is set, `medium.end_tx(tx_id)` and `_drop_delayed_rx_for_tx(tx_id)` (already done via `_drop_delayed_rx_for_node`). Then super can drop the TxEndEvent. Do not leave a Transmission in Medium._active_transmissions after the node is gone. Test: start_transmission, remove_node(tx) during airtime, assert tx.id not in medium.get_active_transmissions at any later time and that len(medium._active_transmissions) does not grow across N add/tx/remove cycles. Receivers must not decode a removed node's frame after end_tx (fail-closed: radio is gone). Keep 9098.22: exit_rx_mode must still not delete TxEnd.
acceptance_criteria: remove_node on a node with an in-flight TX calls medium.end_tx so the Transmission is gone from Medium._active_transmissions and _tx_positions. N add → TX → remove cycles leave the medium list empty (or only other nodes' live TXs). test_remove_node_drops_stash still returns None for a re-added rx id. test_deliver_pending_preserves_tx_end still keeps TxEnd when RX is torn down without remove_node. get_rx_result on a neighbor after remove_node(tx) during that airtime does not deliver the removed node's payload.
